description: Authored examine/take replies for the named forest and foundation locals. No scenery engine.

replacements.old:
<ROUTINE SURFACE-TREE-F ()
	<COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
	       <TELL "The tree is old, deeply rooted, and entirely committed to remaining part of the forest." CR>)
	      (<VERB? LISTEN>
	       <TELL "Branches shift overhead while the trunk contributes the patient silence of wood." CR>)
	      (T <RFALSE>)>>

<ROUTINE SURFACE-SONGBIRD-F ()
replacements.new:
<ROUTINE SURFACE-TREE-F ()
	<COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
	       <TELL "The tree is old, deeply rooted, and entirely committed to remaining part of the forest." CR>)
	      (<VERB? LISTEN>
	       <TELL "Branches shift overhead while the trunk contributes the patient silence of wood." CR>)
	      (<AND <VERB? CLIMB-FOO CLIMB-UP CLIMB-ON>
		    <EQUAL? ,HERE ,NORTH-OF-HOUSE>>
	       <TELL "There is no tree here suitable for climbing." CR>)
	      (T <RFALSE>)>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-NEEDLES-F ()
	<COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
	       <TELL "Old needles make a quiet layer over the soil. They catch at the undergrowth instead of offering a path of their own." CR>)
	      (<VERB? TAKE>
	       <TELL "You scoop a handful. They are only needles, and they fall back where they belong." CR>)
	      (T <RFALSE>)>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-CANOPY-F ()
	<COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
	       <TELL "The canopy thins to the east, enough for a clear wash of sunlight to reach the needles below." CR>)
	      (<VERB? LOOK-UNDER>
	       <TELL "Under the thinning cover the ground is still pine forest, not a new room." CR>)
	      (T <RFALSE>)>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-UNDERSTORY-F ()
	<COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
	       <TELL "Roots and old needles make the ground look easier to cross than the undergrowth actually permits." CR>)
	      (<VERB? CUT>
	       <TELL "This tangle is not the western wall that already yielded to a machete. It is ordinary dim-forest undergrowth, and it stays where it is." CR>)
	      (T <RFALSE>)>>

<ROUTINE HOUSE-FOUNDATION-STONE-F ()
	<COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
	       <TELL "Old foundation stone shows where the painted wall gives way to weeds and the darker edge of the forest. It is part of the house, not a loose rock." CR>)
	      (<VERB? TAKE>
	       <TELL "The foundation is still doing the work of holding the house up." CR>)
	      (T <RFALSE>)>>

<ROUTINE SURFACE-SONGBIRD-F ()
